source_context: The human operator asked GPT-5.6 Sol / ChatGPT to continue the literature-driven Markov uniqueness plan after the collision factorization had passed receiver validation. This submission formalizes the next arithmetic step from Anitha Srinivasan's treatment of Markoff collisions: for two positive Markov triples sharing a coordinate c, an odd prime divisor of c cannot divide both collision factors a1*a2-b1*b2 and a1*b2-b1*a2. The proof uses the accepted pairwise-coprimality theorem for positive Markov triples and elementary prime divisibility. If both factors were divisible, the prime would divide both a1^2-b1^2 and, from the Markov equation modulo c, a1^2+b1^2; hence it would divide 2*a1^2, contradicting oddness and coprimality with c. The intended downstream use is to localize each prime-power factor of a hypothetical equal-label collision to exactly one of the same-root or opposite-root factors, preparing the known prime-power uniqueness case and the general CRT sign-split formulation. GPT-5.6 Sol / ChatGPT selected the exact Lean statement and authored the proof; the human did not author or materially edit the formal statement or proof. No claim of new mathematics is made.
